_comment: The one configuration file for the whole app. Replaces app.config.json.
Three sections, and the split is load-bearing rather than cosmetic:
app    - brand strings. Compiled into the browser bundle.
client - behaviour a deployer might change. Compiled into the bundle.
server - the server's own settings. NEVER reaches the bundle: vite defines
only the app and client sections, so there is nothing for a stray
import to leak, and verify:relay asserts both that no client
source imports this file and that a built dist/ contains none of
these values.
Every key under `server` can be overridden by the environment variable named
beside it, and the environment wins. That is how to set a real secret in
production: leave the placeholder here and set RELAY_SECRET on the host.
This file is committed, so anything written into it is public - the server
warns at startup and refuses to proxy while relaySecret still looks like a
placeholder, because a public secret authenticates nobody.
The server reads this file at runtime, so changing a `server` value needs a
restart but not a rebuild, and config.json must be deployed alongside
server/dist/relay.cjs. The `app` and `client` sections are compiled in, so
changing those needs `npm run build`.
Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation for the key above them
and are ignored.

app.name: InBrowser
app.tagline: The whole AI stack, in one browser tab.
app.description: The whole AI stack in one browser tab. Local models, twelve language runtimes, agents and skills. No account, no API key, no server.
app._organizationName: The publisher named in schema.org Organization. Separate from name so a project and its publisher can differ later without a rename.
app._logoPath: Origin-relative. Becomes the absolute Organization.logo in structured data.
app._locale: BCP 47. Fills <html lang> and og:locale. There is no translated build, so this is the only one.
app._twitterHandle: Without the @. Empty means no twitter:site tag is emitted at all, which is correct - a blank one is worse than none.

client._comment: Compiled into the browser bundle. Never put a secret here.
client._relayUrl: Empty means this deployment's own origin, which is right when the server serves the client. A build hosted on a CDN with no server of its own must set an absolute URL here or the proxy feature has nowhere to go.
client._searchBackend: duckduckgo | serper | jina. The default for a new user; everyone can change it in Settings.
client._streamIdleTimeoutMs: How long a stream may go silent before it is treated as dead. Generous on purpose: it exists to catch a connection that went away without closing, not to enforce a deadline.
client._maxRoutingAttempts: How many models and proxies "auto" may try before giving up on a turn.
client._suggestionsEnabled: Whether the chat empty state fetches its starter prompts from GET /v1/suggestions on this deployment's own server. This is the ONLY first-party API call the client makes on an ordinary page load; it sends a day part and up to three model-capability booleans, and no identifier, chat content or history. Set false for a build hosted on a CDN with no server of its own - it would otherwise request a 404 on every visit - and the suggestion grid is simply not rendered.
client._analyticsId: GA4 Measurement ID, from Google Analytics > Admin > Data Streams (that stream's own id, 15799240062, never appears in code - only the Measurement ID does). Empty disables analytics entirely, which is the default a fork of this repository should keep: without it, a self-hosted deployment would silently report its visitors to InBrowser's own GA property.

server._comment: Server only. Never compiled into the bundle. Each key names the environment variable that overrides it.
server._port: PORT. Production only; development uses devPort.
server._devPort: PORT, the same variable - it overrides whichever of port/devPort applies. Development only: NODE_ENV=production reads `port` instead.
server._workerUrl: WORKER_URL. The Cloudflare Worker that dials proxies (the inbrowser-relay repo). Must be the wss:// scheme and must end in /v1 - the worker answers the tunnel only on that path and 404s everything else, and its /health route is for the Settings test button, not for this. Empty disables proxying - those requests return 503.
server._relaySecret: RELAY_SECRET. Must match the Worker's. Generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`. Leave this empty and set the environment variable in production: this file is committed, so a secret written here is public.
server._allowedOrigins: ALLOWED_ORIGINS, comma-separated. Empty is correct when this server serves the client, because the relay is then same-origin and needs no CORS at all. Set it only for a deployment whose client is hosted elsewhere.
server._maxBodyBytes: MAX_BODY_BYTES. 32 MiB. Caps a proxied upload.
server._rateLimitPerMinute: RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE. Proxied requests per client address per minute.
server._distDir: DIST_DIR. Where the built client lives. Empty means ./dist relative to the working directory, which must be the repo root.
server._metricsPort: METRICS_PORT. Aggregate, non-identifying counters on GET /metrics, always bound to 127.0.0.1 and never reachable through the edge. 0 disables the listener entirely, which is the default: a self-hoster should get the same one-port process the deploy docs describe unless they ask for more.
server._maxInflightTunnels: MAX_INFLIGHT_TUNNELS. Proxied requests this process will hold open at once before answering 503 relay_at_capacity. PER CLUSTER WORKER, not per box - multiply by clusterWorkers. 0 removes the bound, which is how this behaved before admission control existed and is not advisable anywhere a real user can reach. Re-measure with scripts/loadtest-relay.ts before changing it.
server._clusterWorkers: CLUSTER_WORKERS. Worker processes sharing the listening socket. 1 keeps everything in one process. 0 sizes to the box. The motive is not throughput: most CPU at this concurrency goes on per-message work for streamed replies, so a single process means one garbage collection pause stalls every live stream at once. Development always forces 1.
server._poolTunnels: POOL_TUNNELS=1. Reuse a tunnel across requests. Off by default and best left that way - measured hit rate is about 7.5% in the most favourable case and near zero for the workloads that matter, and it is the one setting that affects request isolation. Read the header of server/src/tunnelPool.ts before enabling it.
server._redis: Server only. REDIS_URL, REDIS_PASSWORD (environment only), REDIS_KEY_PREFIX, REDIS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS. Redis is required for new proxy requests and catalog reads.
server._freeProxyCatalog: Server-only scheduled collection. FREE_PROXY_INTERVAL_MINUTES changes the full job cadence after restart. FREE_PROXY_STATE_DIR stores public snapshots; FREE_PROXY_CATALOG_DISABLED=1 disables collection. No public request starts a job.
